Author: @AtomBomb420
Content:
32:36 The cheetah has the same storage space as the shitbox, 5 stacks, so 100 for 20 stacks (jars, product, ingredients), and 50 for 10 stacks (seeds, soil, fertilizer), the veeper has the best storage, and better top speed, with the same acceleration as the shitbox, so just don't buy the shitbox, you aren't gonna be missing anything (trust me I know, I bought it first, and it sucked, I never regretted the veeper, besides, with the veeper and the player, you can hold 3 large shelves worth of items, great for restocking employee shelves and whatnot)

Edit: 55:50 stop wasting money on small deliveries! There is a $200 delivery fee for EACH van sent to a property. Only use deliveries when buying ingredients in bulk, as buying $280 worth of ingredients is a bit wasteful given you are paying nearly double what the ingredients are worth, I did the same exact thing, until I realised I was being scammed of my precious baggies 😂 delivery vans hold 320 items like ingredients, or 160 things like soil (2 large shelves, 16 slots)

Btw, workers don't need tools, meaning you don't have to give your gardeners trimmers or watering cans, you only need to provide seeds, soil, and additives, nothing else, meaning you could sell the trimmers and watering cans when you get everything automated (just always keep money on hand to pay them) or store them in your other unused property, always good to have a plan B

Author: @bradywalker5291
Content:
I think their pathfinding gets broken when the items can't move properly.

My setup has 2 chemists cooking, and 2 mixing. The two mixing have a spare slot each(6 total mixes), but I'm using the spare space for coke. I had preloaded every station, thinking it'd be super fast, but it broke their AI because the products couldn't move(I think) . 

I think the problem is that you have 6 ovens going into one mixer, whereas you should have it go to a shelf, and then have a handler move it to the first mixer in line. Then, of course an output shelf for packaging. 

As for handlers, they can't follow recipes so you gotta set up the labs yourself to avoid the headache. Use that handler for moving the "oven output shelf" to the first mixer, then the final mix ends on a shelf, where the handler moves it to the press. This prevents any back logging, which breaks their AI. Then, you'll need another handler to distribute ingredients for the mix - with the original helping, because they only have 5 routes.

I find it helps to organize your workers by task, rather than having them all scattered about.

Content:
Just a few tips Jack... if u want to use any of these for ur gameplay u can if not no biggie 
- 1st U can unpackage things (if u didn't know!!!) when ur in the packing table click the little arrow that says PACKING (its a blue arrow) it'll turn red and say UNPACKING u can then unpackage products out of jars and bags..to undo this and go back to packing just click it again

-4th tip this one is kind of a "glitch" with the skateboard if u go to say the bus stop or the little overhang over the dumpster outside ur barn and rapidly press space to jump u'll get stuck in the ceiling once u move out from in under whatever ceiling ur under u'll get launched to the sky and can "fly" around on the skateboard once u equip it u'll eventually come back down to earth but u'll have a bunch of momentum to zip around with AND if ur running from the cops u can use this trick to escape them (also u can hide in dumpters WITH LIDS from the cops...they'll never find u) (credit for this glitch goes to GassyMexican he made a whole tiktok showing people how to do it!)

Author: @spartananator4191
Content:
A couple of employee tips: Setting the destination for a station is a very useful tool, It allows you to move a product to a place without using any employee tasks. Botanists are unique because they can have a supplies station, which no other employee can really get, For example, one botanists product destination can be another botanists supplies shelf. (One botanist can grow bud and another can hang it on a drying rack for example, and this whole process can use zero handlers and just two botanists)

Its totally possible to automate the mixing of products with chemists and a few handlers, but you wont be able to have meth AND marijuana production under the same roof unfortunately.

Handlers are best used to move one type of item from one shelf, to one station, in this way they could be used to deliver mixing ingredients from storage to a mixing station, and each mixing station could be set to deliver the finished product to the next mixing station thus automating it.

Author: @Noided88815
Content:
a quick tip, the chemist can move things! use your clip board to set the destination of whatever your chemist is using to either another chemist station or a storage rack. If you set it to another mixer, you can do the same with another chemist. if you do the rack, you'll use the mover. only thing is a chemist can only move things from a chemist station to a rack or another chemist station. they *can not* move things from a storage rack to a station, that's just handlers. 

my favorite use of this is to have a chemist set to use 3 mixers, chain them together, have the mover move ingredients/base drug from the racks onto the mixers, and have the chemist move the drug through them. then just set the last mixers destination to a rack, and have your handler bag it.

(also very good chance you figured this out already i haven't finished the video lol)

Author: @the_ecips9692
Content:
I'm playing with my husband, he does the dealing and I'm cooking :D It's super fun in multiplayer.
We also moved to the barn and we're no min-maxers, but I had  real problems finding a layout that works. Here's 2 minor life hacks for the barn to try:

1. If you put all shelves in the barn on one side (so you can access them from the sides), you get more space for the machines. 
We have the right side of the barn be just shelves and it took us about 4 iterations of moving everything around to fit enough stuff in there.

2. If you park the van in the driveway to the barn (the forest path that connects the road to the barn) facing the road, you can get in, swtich on he headlights (h key) and get out. The light stays on and the van's lights are so strong you see those shinies from half across the town. Makes navigating to the barn in the dark much easier :)

I find that playing for funsies is, well, more fun. There's a lot of "max value products" lists out there and we tried those, but using recipes to min-max everything makes the game a pure grindfest. It's nice for getting cash a bit quicker, but I'm not sure if that's the goal. Automating everything with max efficiency gives you like... nothing to do but afk and sometimes drive stuff to your dealers. Meh. I prefer cookin'!

Edit: If you give the pawn shop dude to a dealer, he's hardly manning his store. We never saw him once, until we got him off the dealer's customer list. Now he's in his store and gets his stuff directly again. When the NPCs get too addicted, they actually don't do their jobs anymore it seems xD
Edit 2: You can make Coca-Mixes that are worth over 700. Per bag. Makes 14k per brick. Plan a planter area, just a tip on the side. :D

Author: @EmotionalSupportChaosDemon
Content:
When you sell to customers you get 20XP, when DEALERS sell to customers you get 10XP, you get 5XP for when you harvest plants and stuff. To a degree the XP is a little unpredictable, but I find the best method to be get multiple stacks of a good selling product in all baggies and then just do around and sell them yourself to anyone and everyone you can. You can also make your most expensive product in EXCESS, and then unassign EVERYONE to dealers, and then list it for sale, and EVERYONE will buy from you, and you will get LOADS of money and xp. (It is stressful though, so be careful, maybe only unassign from 1 of the dealers to give yourself more customers, but not overload and overwhelmed yourself with too many people.)

Also, XP is dependent on SALES, not on AMOUNT, so just go around selling 1-2 to everyone, you still get 20 XP no matter how many you sell.

Content:
to get XP (and money!) most efficiently, unassign all customers from your dealers. then, whenever a customer texts you, set the time for the deal to be "late night". since time never progresses past 4am, the deal cant run out of time unless you go to bed. also, since its night, you get the curfew cash bonus. edit: the reason you sometimes dont get xp after days is because saving and reloading seems to randomly reset all xp progress for that day, so you should probably save before going out to do all those deals so you dont lose any xp.

edit: Oh, just to answer your question: How much XP can I get a day?

The answer varies based on how much effort you put in alongside player amount and other variables. 500 XP a day is a pretty good amount for having 4 dealers and 1 player selling product all day.

XP is based on deals. Dealers earn 10 XP per deal while players earn 20. The amount you deal to a customer matters not, it's the deal itself. Dealers will generally deal once to each of their customers a day at most, so this gives 100 XP per dealer if optimally set up with local customers. The player themselves can easily earn 160 XP a day by selling to 8 other customers either through deals on the phone or selling on the street.

The most XP I've made in a singles day was in the 900 range; all my dealers made 100 XP each (5 at the time) and I myself made over 20 deals.
